about: The country's and the world's yearly CO2, the base the climate engine's carbon laws move, and the path the rest of the world follows.

usEnergyCo2GtPerYear.source: U.S. Energy Information Administration, U.S. energy-related carbon dioxide emissions, 2024 total 4,789 million metric tons (eia.gov/environment/emissions/carbon/).

landUseCo2GtPerYear.source: Global Carbon Budget 2024, Earth System Science Data 17:965 (2025): land-use change 4.2 +/- 2.6 GtCO2 a year, held flat.

usShareOfFossil.source: 4.789 GtCO2 (EIA, 2024) over 37.4 GtCO2 of global fossil CO2 (Global Carbon Budget 2024), held at the 2024 share along the path.

worldFossilOpeningGt.source: Global Carbon Budget 2025 (Global Carbon Project, Nov 2025): 38.1 billion metric tons of fossil CO2 in 2025 (ucdavis.edu/climate/blog/fossil-fuel-co2-emissions-hit-record-high-2025). The opening stock only; no later year is read.

restOfWorldTrendPerYear.spread: Each world draws its own steady yearly change of the rest of the world's fossil CO2 from this span when it opens: IEA current-policies keeps about 38 Gt to 2050 (about 0 a year), stated-policies falls below 30 Gt in 2050 (about -1 a year); the low end is a faster fall than either.
restOfWorldTrendPerYear.source: IEA World Energy Outlook 2025 scenarios (iea.org/reports/world-energy-outlook-2025/stated-policies-scenario, read from a search summary). Only the span of the trend is sourced; no year's value is read.
